correctness.rationale: Two independently structured complete finite enumerations show no connected dominating sets below six and exactly 192 at six, all induced six-vertex paths; every jump is checked by exact set exchange and membership. A full 192-element regular affine even-permutation action and the four base-neighbor generators are explicitly checked. Breadth-first search determines every distance layer and the odd parity-return length 11, proving odd girth. No sliding edge exists. Packaged Python sources implement all exhaustive loops without external data.

originality.rationale: The substantive claim concerns a fixed-cardinality minimum connected-dominating-set jump graph of the four-cube with an explicit affine Cayley identification and full geodesic and odd-girth profile. Inspected nearest publications use addition/deletion, ordinary minimum domination, local sliding, dominating path bounds, or standalone enumeration and do not entail the four-cube exchange graph under stated hypotheses. One most relevant earlier paper is abstract-only, so historical overlap is a genuine residual risk and no publication-priority guarantee is asserted.
residual_risks: The highly relevant 2003 Dvořák–Havel–Mollard full text was not obtained; the abstract cannot exclude a hidden exact classification.
The full text of the 2015 one-movable connected domination article was inaccessible; indexed excerpts concern local slides but do not settle all overlap questions.
An equivalent Cayley-graph or metric treatment may exist in unindexed mathematics or supplementary material; no independent priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: Optimal connected dominating sets model minimum connected coverage backbones. For the natural 4-cube, their full token-jumping reachability and rigidly disconnected sliding contrast is a motivated connectivity question. The nonobvious regular Cayley model and exact radius/diameter/odd-girth give structural information not automatically implied by a configuration count; a finite exact classification is independently useful without extrapolating to all dimensions.
